provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: B2b family batch, rfq archetype. Buyer is a property or facilities manager. Accessibility layout copy describes the client's service only and gives no code advice. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Accessible stall and van-accessible aisle layout, access-aisle hatching, sign posts and wheel stops, and a note that layouts follow the local code the client works to
pageStructurePlus.why: Many restripes start with an accessibility complaint or a landlord inspection. Managers look for a striper who shows the layout work, not just paint.

pageStructurePlus.section: Crack fill, sealcoat and restripe cycle
pageStructurePlus.contains: Which asphalt gets crack fill, patching, sealcoat and fresh lines, in what order, how the cycle repeats by lot traffic, and cure times before cars return
pageStructurePlus.why: Property managers budget asphalt maintenance as a cycle, not a one-off. Showing the cycle turns one sealcoat job into a multi-year plan.

pageStructurePlus.section: Phased lot closure and tenant notices
pageStructurePlus.contains: Section-by-section closure maps, cone and barricade plans, printable tenant and customer notices, and overnight or weekend work windows
pageStructurePlus.why: Retail and office managers worry about closing the lot more than about price. A closure plan on the page answers their first objection.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A request form for faded lines, alligator cracking, potholes, oil spots and standing water, with lot size and photo upload, answered with a scope
pageStructurePlus.why: Managers often oversee lots across town. A photo check lets them start the bid without meeting the striping crew on site.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Re-layout to add stalls, fire lane and curb painting, directional arrows, stall numbers, loading and EV stencils, warehouse floor and court lines
pageStructurePlus.why: The line striping job grows when the buyer sees stencils and re-layout listed. Owners rarely list them, so buyers don't ask.

openers.line: Your Google listing shows a phone number for parking lot striping but no website, so a property manager collecting three asphalt bids has nothing to forward to the owner.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a property manager would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens a Facebook page of fresh lines and sealcoat. A facilities manager wants your lot sizes, closure plan and insurance, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest lot they posted.
openers.linkLine: A sealcoating page built for the facilities buyer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still has a free-host banner and an old service list. Procurement checks the striping contractor's site before they put you on the bid list.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: a builder banner, an old copyright year or a dead form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same asphalt maintenance company, current and complete: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your striping site on my phone and the services menu covered the page. Managers check vendors from the parking lot itself, on a phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same striping company, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask you for a sealcoat bid except calling, and you're on a lot all day. A form asking for lot size, stall count and lot photos would catch those bids.
openers.hook: Check the listing and any site for a bid or quote form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A bid request that asks for lot size and stall count: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after posts of restriped lots are the best sales tool in asphalt maintenance, and they're buried on Facebook where no property manager looks.
openers.hook: Find one before-and-after striping post. Name the lot type if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your lots on a project page a manager can forward: {demo-link}

openers.line: A reviewer wrote that your crew sealcoated their lot overnight and the stores opened on time. That line belongs next to your bid request, not only on a map.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase from a business customer. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews next to the sealcoat bid form: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sealcoating season opens as soon as nights stay warm, and property managers lock their asphalt vendors before then. The ones they can find in late winter get the calls.
openers.hook: Use this in late winter or early spring. Name the month the local sealcoat season usually opens.

openers.line: Your crews stripe lots overnight so stores can open, and the bid calls come in at ten in the morning while you sleep. Those calls go to the next striping company that picks up.
openers.hook: Call their listed number mid-morning. If it goes to voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A striping page that takes the bid while your crew sleeps: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring for a sealcoat crew. Good laborers check whether an asphalt company looks steady before they apply, and a crew page helps you hire faster.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A sealcoating site with a crew hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts show striped lots on both sides of {City}, but there's no page listing the towns and business parks you cover. Managers search asphalt contractors by area.
openers.hook: Find the furthest lot they posted from their base and name the town.
openers.linkLine: Coverage pages for your striping routes: {demo-link}

openers.line: Property managers ask an asphalt contractor about net terms and certificates of insurance before price. If your site answers both, the sealcoat bid gets approved without a call.
openers.hook: Only if they already work for businesses. Check reviews and posts for commercial lots first.
openers.linkLine: Sealcoating terms answered before the bid: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every landlord asks a striping contractor for a certificate of insurance before the crew sets a cone. A page that says you're insured answers it before the walk.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing or posts. Never claim coverage you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and safety on one striping page: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like your sealcoating work comes from a few property managers who know you. When one of them changes jobs, their replacement searches for asphalt vendors instead of calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or posts that mention a property manager or a repeat lot. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a new property manager would find you: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is clean striping work. A lot like that belongs on a project page a manager can send to the owner.
openers.hook: Pick their newest lot post and name it: the property type and whether it was sealcoat, restripe or both.
openers.linkLine: That lot on a striping project page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is clean striping work.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the Facebook page, but nothing a property manager could forward to an owner. I put together a sample asphalt maintenance page with a lot-size bid request and a closure plan section, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample striping and sealcoating site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a bid request with lot size and stall count, a sealcoat and restripe cycle, and a page for insurance and tenant notices. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.

IF NO:
"Easy to miss when you're on a lot. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a bid request for lot size and stall count and a phased closure section, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a striping company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is about one mid-size sealcoat job."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, on a rain day if that's easier?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: My work comes from property managers who already know me.
objections.handler: "Good, keep them. The site is for the day one of them moves on and the new manager searches for a sealcoating contractor instead of calling."

objections.objection: It's the middle of sealcoat season, I've got no time.
objections.handler: "Then I'll do it from your posts and a twenty-minute call on a rain day. It's live before the spring bids next year."

objections.objection: Paving companies send me all my striping.
objections.handler: "Then the site keeps a second source open. Managers who only need a restripe don't call a paver, they search striping."

objections.objection: Winter is dead for me, I can't spend now.
objections.handler: "Winter is when managers set next year's asphalt budget. A site that goes live in the slow months catches those bid lists."

objections.objection: We bid on public jobs through the portal, not websites.
objections.handler: "The portal brings the bid. The evaluator still opens your site to check lot experience, insurance and crew size before they score it."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a bid request, a sealcoat cycle page and coverage pages. That's about one small lot restripe."

sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — property managers in {City} start setting next season's asphalt budgets about now. Thought of you.

The striping and sealcoat page is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one mid-size sealcoat job, never to a single restripe of a small lot.
The bid request with lot size, stall count and photo upload is the core. Price everything else as additions.
Price project pages by lot, not by page: each lot gets a before, an after and a scope line.
Charge for the closure plan and tenant notice kit separately; retail and office managers value it most.
Sell in late winter. A site that lands mid-season gets built on rain days and goes slowly.
Keep monthly add-ons small next to one restripe, so nobody questions them in the slow months.

lineItems.item: Lot bid request with photo upload
lineItems.description: Max with lot size, stall count, surface condition checkboxes, closure window and a map pin for each lot.
Max when each lot gets before and after shots, the scope performed and the closure plan used.
Max with a cycle diagram by lot traffic, cure times and a printable maintenance plan a manager can budget from.
Max with editable notice templates, a phased closure map layout and a re-open time banner per job.
Max when it carries the equipment list, coverage, insurance summary and references the client supplies.
Max when each page names the business parks and retail centers served in that town.
Max with every stencil they carry, a re-layout request and examples of fire lanes, curbs and warehouse lines.

whatElseYouSell.name: Property manager mailing for asphalt season
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each month in late winter, a short note to the property managers near your lots, pointing at the sealcoat bid request."
whatElseYouSell.when: Late winter, once the bid request is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for striping work
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every restriped lot goes on your Google profile the week it's done, so the listing looks as busy as your striping season is."

whatElseYouSell.name: Drone lot photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Fresh lines only look right from above. One morning of overhead shots on finished lots gives the asphalt site its best proof."
whatElseYouSell.when: Mid-season, on lots the owners agree to in writing, with a licensed drone operator.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring sealcoat pre-booking campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before the first warm week, a campaign offering early sealcoat slots to every lot you did two seasons ago."

whatElseYouSell.name: Bid packet design for asphalt maintenance
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every striping and sealcoat bid goes out with the same packet: scope by lot section, closure plan, insurance summary and references."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or before a bid deadline they mention.

whatElseYouSell.name: Reference and review collection from managers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When a lot reopens on time, the manager gets a short review request and a reference letter draft for your next sealcoat bid."

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck, trailer and cone artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A sealcoat rig parked in a lot all night is a billboard. Matching truck lettering, trailer panels and stenciled cones make it read as one company."

withoutAI.whoPays: The paving company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who does the patching and overlays on lots you stripe? Pavers need the same bid page you have."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pavers and stripers trade lots back and forth and already send each other work.

withoutAI.route: Property management firms whose lots they maintain
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The manager who hires your striping crew has a tenant portal from years ago. I can rebuild it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust vendors who reopen their lots on time. A striper's introduction gets the meeting.

withoutAI.whoPays: The sweeping company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The sweeper that clears your lots before you sealcoat faces the same property manager. I build their site on the same layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same lots, same buyer, and they work the same nights.

withoutAI.route: Snow plowing contractors on the same lots
withoutAI.whoPays: The plow contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Plow blades chew up your stripes every winter. The plow contractor on those lots needs a seasonal contract page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Plow contractors and stripers share lots and managers, and their seasons don't overlap.

withoutAI.route: The sealer and line paint supply yard
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your sealer and paint supplier sells to every striping crew in the region with a price sheet nobody can find. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards have budgets, and their contractor list is the prospect list you'd otherwise build by hand.

withoutAI.route: Retail center and church facilities committees
withoutAI.whoPays: The center owner or the church
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The church whose lot you just sealcoated has an events page nobody updates. Your introduction gets me in the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Facilities committees trust the contractor who just made their lot look new.

withAI.route: Photo-based patch estimate for the paving sub
withAI.pitchLine: "Managers upload pothole and cracking photos with a rough lot size, and the paver gets a draft asphalt patch estimate."
withAI.whyItWorks: Pavers lose days driving to small patch jobs. A draft estimate filters them first.

withAI.route: Tenant notice assistant for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "The manager enters the lot section and the closure night, and the assistant drafts every tenant notice and reminder for the restripe."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers dread tenant complaints about lot closures. Cutting that work is easy to approve.

withAI.route: Reorder assistant for the sealer supply yard
withAI.pitchLine: "Striping crews tell the assistant which lots are booked this week, and it drafts the sealer, sand and line paint order."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps contractors ordering from one yard, which is worth more to the yard than a discount.

withAI.route: Seasonal quote assistant for the plow contractor
withAI.pitchLine: "The plow contractor on your lots quotes from lot size and curb count. An assistant drafts the seasonal plowing quote from a map pin."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built once around the lots your striping client already knows, sold through their trust.

withAI.route: Sweeping schedule assistant for retail centers
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants report litter or spills in the parking lot, and the assistant logs it and books the sweeper's next pass."
withAI.whyItWorks: Center owners want fewer tenant calls, and the striper is already the vendor they trust with the lot.

withAI.route: Lot condition summaries for HOA boards
withAI.pitchLine: "Board members get a plain-language summary of each community parking lot's cracking, fading and sealcoat timing before the budget meeting."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards approve asphalt work faster when they understand it, and the striper's photos feed the summary.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for sealcoat bids
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A manager calls while you're rolling sealer, gets a text asking for the lot address and stall count, and you call back with the bid half done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Sealcoat and striping bid calculator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter square footage, stall count, crack fill footage and stencils, and the calculator drafts the asphalt bid from your own rates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before sealcoat season. Needs their production rates, material costs and margin rules.

softwareAI.name: Lot measurement from a map outline
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Trace the parking lot on an aerial map, and the tool gives square footage and linear feet of striping before you drive out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a map data account they own and a few past lots to check the measurements against.

softwareAI.name: Bid writer from lot walk notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the lot walk in the truck: cracks, faded stalls, the closure window. A draft sealcoat bid is waiting when you get back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, after the calculator. Needs past bids and their scope wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Weather-based reschedule alerts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When rain or a cold night is forecast for a booked sealcoat, the manager and the tenants get the new date before you have to call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the job calendar, their temperature and rain rules and manager contacts.

softwareAI.name: Maintenance cycle tracker per lot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every lot's last sealcoat, restripe and crack fill date in one place, with the next one flagged before the manager's budget meeting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs two seasons of job records by lot address.

softwareAI.name: Closure notice writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick the lot sections and the night, and it drafts the tenant notice, the door sign and the reminder text for the striping job."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their notice wording and closure rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Manager portal with lot history and invoices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Property managers log in to see every lot's sealcoat history, before and after shots and invoices, without emailing you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once several managers send repeat work. Needs the lot tracker and their invoice records.

softwareAI.name: Daytime receptionist for overnight striping crews
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers the striping line while the night crew sleeps, takes the lot address and closure window and books the lot walk."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar, coverage and the questions they ask on every bid call. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew and rig scheduling board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which sealcoat rig and striping machine go to which lot tonight, with material loads and cure times in one board."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, when they run more than one crew. Needs the equipment list and the season's job list.

softwareAI.name: Lot photo condition grader
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A manager uploads lot photos, and it sorts the asphalt into crack fill, patch, sealcoat or restripe for the owner to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a few hundred graded lot photos from their own jobs and the owner's review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sealcoat renewal reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a lot's sealcoat cycle comes due, the manager gets a reminder with last job's photos and an early booking slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the lot tracker dates and manager contacts.

softwareAI.name: Material usage and job costing per lot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which lots made money once sealer, paint, crew nights and travel are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs crew hours and material use per job for one season.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for asphalt customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every review of a sealcoated or restriped lot gets a reply in your voice, ready for you to approve from the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review collection. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Invoicing with net-terms follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The sealcoat invoice goes out the morning after the lot reopens, and accounts payable gets a polite nudge when terms run out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their accounting system and each manager's billing terms.

softwareAI.name: Stencil and stall layout planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sketch the re-layout on the lot outline: stall rows, accessible spaces, arrows and fire lanes, then send the drawing to the manager for sign-off."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the lot measurement tool and the client's layout standards.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot for sealcoat timing and closure questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'how long before cars can park' and 'can you do it in sections' from your real cure times, then books the lot walk."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their service list, cure times and closure rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Public bid tracker for asphalt work
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads the city, county and school bid notices each week and flags striping and sealcoating work in your area with the due date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the list of portals they're registered on and their coverage. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Night crew check-in with lot photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Crews check in at each lot and snap the finished lines before they leave, so the manager sees the striping done by morning."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs crew phones and the lot list.

softwareAI.name: Crew safety briefing translator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each lot's traffic plan, cone layout and sealer handling notes, translated for every crew member before the shift."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their written lot instructions and review by a bilingual foreman. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the lot bid calculator for striping contractors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a sealcoat and striping calculator for one contractor. Every asphalt crew prices lots on a napkin."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client taught you the production math and paid for the build. Every market has the same problem.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor finder licensed to a sealer manufacturer's distributors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-a-sealcoater map on your site for every striping crew that buys from your yards. They stay loyal to the yard that sends them lots."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on contractor loyalty. A map that sends asphalt jobs is stickier than a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member a sealcoat bid page and a lot closure kit as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one deal reaches many asphalt owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each striping territory needs coverage pages and a bid request that routes to the right owner. I build the lot template once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract, many territories, one template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Vendor scheduling portal for a retail property owner
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Sealcoat, sweeping, plowing and lighting vendors post their lot schedules to one portal across all your centers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owners juggle lot vendors across many centers. The striper's workflow is the proof you understand it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label asphalt site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up sealcoating clients and builds from scratch. License my lot bid template instead."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the striping layout you already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same striping kit in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New asphalt clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one parking lot striping company per area. Yours is set in {City}. The next metro over is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the lot photos as proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Lot maintenance planner for HOA management firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community parking lot and private street on one sealcoat and restripe calendar, ready for the reserve study meeting."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: HOA firms manage dozens of lots and buy tools that make board meetings shorter.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Facility services groups bundling exterior trades
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You sell sweeping, striping, plowing and landscaping under one contract. One bid page per trade, one lot request for all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups that bundle exterior trades buy sites in sets and renew them together.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Sealcoat cost estimator sponsored by contractors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Managers estimate a parking lot sealcoat from a map outline, and the sponsoring asphalt company gets the bid request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It uses only the sponsor's own rates, so it never claims market data, and sends the sponsor ready bids.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your sealcoat estimating or scheduling tool and disappeared. I've shipped that lot workflow before."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded clients already decided to buy. They need someone who already knows the asphalt workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Municipal and school district lot programmes
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The striping contractor, per bid packet
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "School and city lots go out to bid every summer. I package the striping capability statement for each public bid."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Public bids repeat every year with the same requirements, so the packet sells again each season.

upsellLadder.trigger: The season ends and they have a full year of lot records to work from.

upsellLadder.line: "The lots due for sealcoat this spring get first pick of dates before the season fills."

upsellLadder.offer: Manager portal with lot history and invoices
upsellLadder.trigger: A property manager with several lots asks for a history of the work done.
upsellLadder.line: "Your biggest manager wants a record of every lot. Give them a portal and the asphalt contract renews itself."
